observation.visible_scene: A woman with long dark hair, wearing a sleeveless blue knotted top, denim shorts and black thigh-high boots, stands with her back to a stationary camera in a bright white dance studio, facing a full-wall mirror; her front-facing reflection occupies the right portion of the frame. Background elements (ceiling track lights, a wall-mounted air-conditioner, a curtain, mirror seams, light wood floor) remain fixed throughout, indicating no camera motion.
visible_changes: The woman's arms move through a repeating dance sequence: one arm alternates between a bent position near the shoulder/face and an extended position out to the side, while the other arm shifts between hanging low and being raised with the elbow bent up toward the head (most clearly in the final frames).

The mirror reflection continuously mirrors these arm positions (e.g., an arm extended to the side in the back view appears as a horizontally extended arm across the chest in the reflection); it is the same person's image, not a second dancer.
Her weight shifts between the two boots: the feet rotate and the heel of one boot lifts at intervals, producing a small stepping/rocking motion in place rather than travel across the floor.
The knotted tail of her top swings between positions (to the right, hanging down, to the left) as her torso rotates slightly.
The overall horizontal position of the body in the frame stays roughly constant; the changes are postural/limb movements, not translation.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether these movements belong to a choreographed routine and what precedes or follows this excerpt.
Any music or audio driving the motion.
The start or completion of any step, since both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
uncertain_details: The exact hand gestures (pointing vs. waving vs. brushing the head) are ambiguous at this frame rate.
Whether the torso itself rotates or only the arms move is not fully resolved.
The precise footwork pattern (pivot vs. side step) cannot be determined from the sampled frames.
Fine left-right correspondence between each real arm and its reflected image is hard to track reliably across the whole clip.
